When I was 9 she taught us how to use the washing machine because my brother started playing football and she couldn't be troubled to clean a pair of pants every other day. Admittedly this was ultimately good as in high school when all my peers were getting ready for college I found out most were just learning how to do their own laundry.

The biggest problem is drinking. She is an alcoholic, and it's gotten worse over time. Spilt beer on my Pokemon cards and homework, vomiting at the dinner table, passing out on the front porch, repeated attempts to make me drink, black out public intoxication on my brother's 21st birthday, semi regular raving around the house. My family is a mix of two cultures with great drinking tradition, and I love the science and history of alcohol, but I'll never touch the stuff for fear of becoming that. Over her children. Over us. Over me.

A normal vehicle will convert 20-30% of the energy in gasoline into motion.

A natural gas electric generating turbine gets 40% efficiency. A high voltage transformer gets 90% efficiency. A household level transformer gets 50% efficiency. A short transmission line gets 20% loss, which is 80% efficiency. The total is 40% x 90% x 50% x 80% = 14.4% of the electrical energy recovered (85.6% lost) before getting to the vehicle and doing something similar to the gasoline engine in the vehicle.

Some other things to consider for this analysis:

  • Internal combustion engines are 20-30% thermodynamically efficient - actual mechanical fuel-to-wheels efficiency is much lower.

  • No-one uses a 50% efficient "household level transformer" to charge an electric car. Solid state chargers are over 90% efficient, up to 98% for newer ones.

  • It ignores the energy required to produce, refine and transport the fuel for internal combustion vehicles (while counting the analogous distribution losses against electric vehicles).

  • It ignores renewables for vehicle charging. Energy payback time for solar generation is 4-5 years these days, after which your vehicle is literally free to charge.

Basically this reads like something written by someone trying to justify their dislike for electric vehicles, rather than like a genuine attempt to compare electric with fuel powered vehicles.

Exactly. Even when charged off coal sourced electricity, an EV produces 40gms of carbon per Km. An efficient ICEV will produce around 120gms. That doesn't seem like much of a difference but once you include the energy needed to produce the fuel the number goes up to around 500gms so an EV charged off the dirtiest fuel available still produces <10% of the emissions that an ICEV will. Also, an ICEV used in a city centre produces a lot more pollution due to the lack of efficiency in slow moving traffic. This is where hybrids are better but still not ideal, whereas an EV with a range extender ICE is optimal at the moment unless you can live with the limitations of a pure BEV (typically max around 100 miles per charge) but they're easily the best for use in a city. Legislation will likely force any ICEV out of cities in coming years. This is already happening in some of the most polluted cities.
